description: The four RFC 5424 §6.5 example log lines, committed verbatim. A syslog line is RFC text, not capturable wire bytes, so the honest source is the RFC's own normative examples — the PRI bit-unpack, NILVALUE handling, and SD-ELEMENT walk are the parser's computation over these exact characters, never an authored answer key. The leading \uFEFF on ex1/ex3 MSG is the real UTF-8 BOM (RFC 5424 §6.4). PRIVAL 34 -> Facility 4 (security/authorization), Severity 2 (Critical); PRIVAL 165 -> Facility 20 (local4), Severity 5 (Notice).

provenance.source: RFC 5424 (The Syslog Protocol), §6.5 Examples; §6.2.1 Table 1 (Facility) + Table 2 (Severity); §6.2.x field defs; §6.3 STRUCTURED-DATA; §6.4 MSG/BOM.
provenance.authored_with_citation: Transcribed verbatim from RFC 5424 §6.5. The 'BOM' placeholder the RFC prints in ex1/ex3 is rendered here as the real U+FEFF byte sequence (EF BB BF) it stands for.
provenance.cross_checked_against: The arithmetic PRIVAL = Facility*8 + Severity verified locally with python3 (divmod): 34 -> (4,2), 165 -> (20,5), matching RFC 5424 §6.2.1's own worked statements ('local use 4 with Severity Notice = 165'). The parser (web/src/engines/visual/syslog.ts) tokenizes these exact lines; web/tests/syslog-fidelity.test.ts asserts its decode equals these RFC-true values, so the parser cannot drift from the spec without CI failing.
provenance.honesty_note: Nothing here is invented. A learner can paste any line into a reference RFC 5424 parser (e.g. rsyslog/syslog-ng test harness) or compute the offsets by hand against §6 and get the identical decode.

broken.honesty_note: A real RFC 5424 line built from ex1 with only the PRIVAL changed 34->39 (same Facility 4, Severity downgraded 2->7). The parser computes the divergent Severity from the real PRI byte — the break is the dissector's arithmetic, not an authored verdict. PRIVAL 39 = 4*8+7 = Facility 4, Severity 7 (Debug), which a Critical-threshold alert never fires on.
